level: stop-fence slice 4, declared Agent pairing-client revocation blocks outside Hosts and unused pre-issued grants; component evidence only
componentAcceptance: Win11: a real independent Agent accepts one complete outside-Host remote-write before revocation. After the real local dsh-remote-agent revoke CLI persistently revokes the declared host client, the Agent stays alive but an already-issued, not-yet-executed fs_write grant receives HTTP 401 AUTH_INVALID and a new outside Host cannot pair with the old long-lived secret. Neither blocked path creates its target file or an operation row; the original succeeded operation receipt remains the only row.
productAcceptance: None. This is admission fencing for one explicitly declared Agent dataDir and clientId. It does not drain an effect already executing at revocation, cover other clients or machines, stop direct OS writers, wire the local CLI into deployment/migration orchestration, or prove activation/rollback. Scores remain 0/20, 1/63 and M0 11/12; stopWriteProvable, activationSupported and postActivationRollbackSupported remain false.
implementation: The test reuses the existing production Agent admin CLI and Store.revoke/currentClient authorization path rather than introducing another fence protocol.

A complete outside Host first writes before-revoke.txt through remote-write. A separate fs_write grant is then issued with the long-lived client secret but deliberately not executed before revocation.
The real CLI revokes host while the independent Agent remains running. The pre-issued grant then receives HTTP 401 AUTH_INVALID at /mcp, and existing-grant.txt is absent.
A second complete outside Host using the old secret fails during pairing with AUTH_INVALID, never submits its Task and never creates after-revoke.txt.

A direct operation-table check retains exactly the original fs_write succeeded receipt, proving neither refused request reached operation admission. The new native suite is registered in npm test; no product source behavior changed.
testRuns: New suite: three consecutive standalone runs, each 1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail.
New suite + outside-Job negative + remote-auth: 12 tests / 12 pass / 0 fail.
Final npm test: phase one 1587/1583/0/4 and phase two 350/270/0/80; total 1937 tests, 1853 pass, 0 fail, 84 skipped.
preservedFailures: The first run waited 20 seconds for the second Host error because the fixture writes a plain UTF-8 stack while the test incorrectly waited for JSON. Reading the actual text exposed AUTH_INVALID immediately; no product behavior or assertion was weakened.
limitations: The revocation boundary is one declared Agent dataDir and clientId. Other clients, other machines, direct filesystem writers and unknown launchers are outside this evidence.
The pre-issued grant had not started its effect. This test does not prove that an operation already executing when revocation occurs is drained or stopped.
The CLI is a local machine administration surface. Remote deployment invocation, migration-orchestrator wiring, failure recovery and rotate/reauthorization remain open.
Loopback synthetic processes are not a cross-machine production deployment or reboot test.
No real user profile, model inference, production process, push or release was used.
